content:
Jess: Quick sync — we need a final decision on span sampling for OTLP exporters. Hosted customers (tiered retention) + Dedicated/private will have different cost/retention needs. Proposal: head sampling at the SDK for low-cost routes, tail sampling in collector for error/critical trace retention, and dynamic sampling rules keyed by route+customer_tier. Thoughts?

Marco: I like the split. Two implementation q's: 1) how do we make tail sampling scalable (can't keep every trace in memory), 2) how do we preserve sampling decision across exporters so different backends can get consistent views?

Rachel: From Console POV, we need deterministic behavior per route & per tenant so dashboards and alerting don't shift day-to-day. Also want easy override for canary rollouts.

Anya: For tail we probably want a policy engine in the collector that only buffers traces for a short window and uses scoring rules (error/span count/latency) to promote. We can use LRU + reservoir sampling per-tenant. Drawback: complexity + ops cost.

Sam: Could we instead use sticky probabilistic sampling at SDK level based on traceID hash + route weight? That gives deterministic sampling per-trace and is cheap. Then do an "upsample" path: any span with error flag gets exported regardless of sample.

Marco: Upsample on error is good but we still lose context for traces where error shows later (downstream service). Tail sampling catches that. Maybe hybrid: head sampling for general traffic + a lightweight tail sampler that only looks at sampled traces' children to decide to promote whole trace?

Kevin: Ops constraints: our collector instances are multi-tenant and memory-limited. Full tail sampling per-tenant isn't feasible unless we route high-tier tenants to dedicated collectors. Could make tail sampling a premium feature for enterprise/dedicated customers.

Jess: That aligns with the biz model. For hosted free/standard tiers: deterministic head sampling (route + tenant weight). For enterprise/dedicated: enable tail sampling with configurable buffer size & rules. Need to design config schema.

Marco: Draft config idea (collector):
```json
{
  "sampling": {
    "mode": "tail",
    "buffer_ms": 2000,
    "per_tenant_reservoir_size": 2000,
    "promote_rules": [
      {"match": "span.attributes.http.status_code >= 500", "action": "promote"},
      {"match": "span.duration_ms > 2000", "action": "promote"}
    ]
  }
}
```
This is rough but shows buffer window + rules.
content_continued:
Rachel: UX: console should show current sampling rate per-route and an "explain sample" link (why a trace was kept/dropped). Also a simple toggle for canary higher-sampling.

Anya: Two more nitpicks: 1) preserve sampling_priority in trace context so exporters can apply downstream logic, 2) ensure exporters annotate which spans were sampled vs dropped.

Sam: On exporters: we need different export streams. Example: high-retention backend (raw traces) for enterprise, aggregated/rollup for low-tier (e.g., count events, 95p latency). Exporter config should support per-backend sampling overrides.

Marco: Implementation approach: SDK does deterministic head sampling with keys: hash(traceID + route + tenant_salt) % 10000 < rate*100. Collector subscribes to all traces but only buffers if tail mode enabled for that tenant. Use a small in-memory ring and async writer to exporters.

Kevin: Cost-control: for hosted customers we should also emit sampling diagnostics metrics (sampled_spans, dropped_spans, promoted_spans) per-route/tenant so billing + alerts can detect anomalies. Keep retention of those metrics long.

Jess: Good. Action items: 1) Marco/Anya prototype collector tail buffer w/ promo rules (ETA 2 weeks), 2) Sam build deterministic SDK sampler impl + docs + deterministic seed per-tenant (ETA 1 week), 3) Rachel design Console panel for sampling rates & canary override (mock by EOW). Kevin: add op budget constraints and admin toggles.

telemetry-bot: Rollout checklist created: TICKET-4532 sampling-policy for OTLP exporters. Assigned: Marco, Sam, Rachel.

Sam: small example of deterministic sampler pseudocode:
```go
func Keep(traceID, route, tenantSalt string, rate float64) bool {
  h := sha256(traceID+route+tenantSalt)
  v := int(binary.BigEndian.Uint32(h[:4]))
  return (v % 1000000) < int(rate*10000)
}
```

Anya: Edge case: distributed traces across private deployments — need to ensure tenant_salt is consistent across services (env config) else sampling will be inconsistent. Add checks in our SDK init.

Marco: Also note: tail sampling increases latency for decision window if we wait for downstream spans. We'll only buffer a short ms window; if not promoted, we drop. Might miss long-tail faults. Tradeoff documented.

Rachel: For canaries: implement temporary "force_sample" tag that console writes to route config. SDK reads and forces sampling for those routes for X minutes. Good for debugging.

Jess: Sounds like a plan. I'll sync with Product on pricing tiers for tail sampling and get legal on retention SLAs. If no objections, I'll merge the RFC and we can start work. :thumbsup:

Kevin: sgtm

Marco: +1
